### Foundations

| Lvl | Note | Type | Summary |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| L1 | [DNS](00-foundations/networking/dns.md) | guide | DNS turns a name into an address. Every answer is cached with an expiry, and there is no way to recall a cached answer early — which explains almost every DNS problem you will meet. |
| L1 | [Linux Basics](00-foundations/linux/linux-basics.md) | guide | Almost every server, container and cloud instance you will ever touch runs Linux — so this is the layer underneath everything else in these notes. |
| L1 | [Networking Basics](00-foundations/networking/networking-basics.md) | guide | Every "it can't connect" problem is one of four things: wrong address, wrong port, a firewall, or nothing listening. |
| L1 | [SSH](00-foundations/linux/ssh.md) | guide | SSH is how you reach every server you will ever manage — and once `~/.ssh/config` is set up, it becomes one short word instead of a long command. |

### DevOps

| Lvl | Note | Type | Summary |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| L1 | [Git](01-devops/git/git.md) | guide | Git tracks snapshots of your whole project, not changes to individual files — once that clicks, most of Git stops being confusing. |
| L2 | [CI/CD](01-devops/ci-cd/ci-cd.md) | guide | CI answers "did this change break anything?" CD answers "can this change reach users safely?" They are different problems and people conflate them constantly. |
| L2 | [Jenkins](01-devops/ci-cd/jenkins.md) | guide | Jenkins is a job runner with an enormous plugin ecosystem — which is both why it survives everywhere and why every neglected Jenkins becomes a liability. |
| L3 | [GitOps](01-devops/ci-cd/gitops.md) | concept | The cluster pulls its desired state from Git instead of a pipeline pushing into the cluster — which turns "what is deployed?" from an investigation into a `git log`. |

### Containers

| Lvl | Note | Type | Summary |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| L1 | [Docker](02-containers/docker/docker.md) | guide | Docker packages an application together with everything it needs to run, so the same package behaves identically on your laptop and in production. |
| L2 | [Docker Images and Registries](02-containers/images/docker-images.md) | guide | An image is a stack of read-only layers. Understanding that one fact explains build caching, image size, and why deleted secrets are still in there. |

### Kubernetes

| Lvl | Note | Type | Summary |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| L1 | [Kubernetes Basics](03-kubernetes/fundamentals/kubernetes-basics.md) | guide | You describe what you want running; Kubernetes keeps making reality match that description. Everything else is detail. |
| L2 | [ConfigMaps and Secrets](03-kubernetes/configmaps/configmaps-and-secrets.md) | guide | Both are key-value objects that decouple configuration from images. The only real difference is that a Secret is base64-encoded and handled slightly more carefully — it is **not** encrypted by default. |
| L2 | [Helm](03-kubernetes/helm/helm.md) | guide | Helm is a templating engine plus a release ledger. Separating those two jobs in your head explains every Helm problem you will have. |
| L2 | [Ingress and TLS](03-kubernetes/ingress/ingress.md) | guide | An Ingress object is a set of routing rules that does nothing on its own. A **controller** has to be installed to read it — and "my Ingress is ignored" is almost always that it is not. |
| L2 | [Kubernetes Deployments](03-kubernetes/deployments/kubernetes-deployments.md) | guide | A Deployment is how you get zero-downtime updates: it never edits a running pod, it creates new ones and removes old ones in a controlled order. |
| L2 | [Kubernetes Pods](03-kubernetes/pods/kubernetes-pods.md) | guide | A pod is not "a container" — it is a small group of containers that share an IP address and a filesystem, and always live and die together. |
| L2 | [Kubernetes Services](03-kubernetes/services/kubernetes-services.md) | guide | Pods get a new IP address every time they restart, so nothing can talk to them directly. A Service is the stable address that stays put. |
| L2 | [Kubernetes Troubleshooting](03-kubernetes/troubleshooting/kubernetes-troubleshooting.md) | troubleshooting | Three commands solve most problems: `describe` tells you what Kubernetes thinks, `logs` tells you what the app said, `get endpoints` tells you why traffic is not arriving. |
| L3 | [Autoscaling and Scheduling](03-kubernetes/autoscaling/autoscaling-and-scheduling.md) | guide | Autoscaling adds pods; the scheduler decides where they go; the cluster autoscaler adds machines when there is nowhere. Three separate systems, and most "autoscaling is broken" is really one of the other two. |
| L3 | [Building a Cluster with kops](03-kubernetes/cluster-maintenance/kops-cluster-setup.md) | runbook | kops treats a cluster as a declarative object stored in S3 — you edit the spec, then tell it to make reality match, which is exactly the Kubernetes model applied to the cluster itself. |
| L3 | [Kubernetes Architecture](03-kubernetes/architecture/kubernetes-architecture.md) | architecture | Nothing in Kubernetes calls anything. Every component watches the API server for a gap between what you asked for and what exists, then acts to close it — and that single sentence explains the whole system. |
| L3 | [Kubernetes RBAC](03-kubernetes/rbac/kubernetes-rbac.md) | guide | Four object types and one rule: permissions are **purely additive**, there is no deny. If someone can do something they should not, you remove a binding — you cannot add a rule to stop them. |
| L3 | [Kubernetes Storage](03-kubernetes/storage/kubernetes-storage.md) | guide | A PVC is a **request** for storage; a PV is the storage itself. You write the request, the cluster finds or creates the disk, and separating those two roles is what makes storage portable between clouds. |
| L3 | [StatefulSets, DaemonSets and Jobs](03-kubernetes/statefulsets/kubernetes-workloads.md) | guide | A Deployment assumes its pods are interchangeable. The other three workload types exist for the cases where they are not — because they have identity, because you need one per node, or because they are meant to finish. |

### Observability

| Lvl | Note | Type | Summary |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| L2 | [Grafana](08-observability/grafana/grafana.md) | guide | Grafana stores no data. It queries other systems and draws the answer — which is why "Grafana is broken" is almost always the datasource or the query. |
| L2 | [Observability Fundamentals](08-observability/metrics/observability-fundamentals.md) | concept | Monitoring tells you **that** something is wrong. Observability is whether you can work out **why** without shipping new code — and the difference is what you can ask, not how many dashboards you have. |
| L2 | [Prometheus](08-observability/prometheus/prometheus.md) | guide | Prometheus does not receive metrics — it goes and fetches them, on a timer, and that one design decision explains almost everything else about it. |

## Find it by the problem you have

Sometimes you know the symptom, not the topic.

| I need to… | Start at |
|:---|:---|
| Debug a pod that will not start | [Kubernetes Troubleshooting](03-kubernetes/troubleshooting/kubernetes-troubleshooting.md) |
| Work out why a Service gets no traffic | [Kubernetes Services](03-kubernetes/services/kubernetes-services.md) |
| Triage a slow or broken Linux box | [Linux Command Cheat Sheet](14-cheat-sheets/linux/linux-commands.md) |
| Remember a `kubectl` flag | [kubectl Cheat Sheet](14-cheat-sheets/kubernetes/kubectl-commands.md) |
| Fix "connection refused" or a timeout | [Networking Basics](00-foundations/networking/networking-basics.md) |
| Understand why a DNS change has not taken effect | [DNS](00-foundations/networking/dns.md) |
| Fix `Permission denied (publickey)` | [SSH](00-foundations/linux/ssh.md) |
| Undo something in Git | [Git](01-devops/git/git.md) |
| Make a Docker build faster or smaller | [Docker Images and Registries](02-containers/images/docker-images.md) |
| Deploy without downtime | [Kubernetes Deployments](03-kubernetes/deployments/kubernetes-deployments.md) |
| Stop a pipeline lying about a failed deploy | [CI/CD](01-devops/ci-cd/ci-cd.md) |
| Avoid destroying infrastructure by accident | [Terraform](05-infrastructure-as-code/terraform/terraform.md) |
